summary: Created a verify-and-close-gaps plan (5 phases, 1.75h) for the already-committed Playwright MCP activation work. Planning-time verification found the research report's flagged 'cannot run the doc-lint gate' blocker is false (the gate runs against the source store via a documented REPO_ROOT override) and that running it surfaces a real FAIL: index-entries.json line_count drift for project/web/README.md (declared 110, actual 116). Also found the invented tool name browser_verify_text_visible surviving as usable guidance in the git-tracked .opencode/extensions/web copy, which the plan handles as an evidenced decision phase rather than an out-of-scope edit.

memory_candidates.content: When a research dispatch exceeds its role and performs implementation edits, the follow-on plan must be a verify-and-close-gaps plan built against the files on disk, not against the research report's claims about them. Independently re-verify the report's assertions before planning: in the Playwright-MCP web-extension activation, two of the report's claims failed verification. It flagged check-extension-docs.sh as unrunnable from the source-store tree, but the script's EXT_DIR defaults to $REPO_ROOT/agent-system/extensions (it lints the SOURCE store, not the deploy tree) and its header documents an explicit 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd)' override for deliberate source-store invocation. Running it then surfaced a real FAIL the report asserted did not exist: a Rule R index-entries.json line_count mismatch caused by the report's own README edit adding lines without updating the declared count. General lesson: a self-reported 'gate could not be run' blocker is a hypothesis to test, not a fact to plan around, and any prose edit to an indexed context file must be paired with a line_count update (verify via generate-context-line-counts.sh --check, scoped read-only; --write rewrites every extension).
